title: Episode 120: C++ Safety, Tuples & Variants with Zach Laine! (Part 4)

sentences.en: You know how they refer to a Hilbert curve as a space-filling curve?
sentences.zh: 你知道他们把希尔伯特曲线称为空间填充曲线吗？

sentences.en: I like to refer to Bryce as an authority-filling curve.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把 Bryce 称为“权威填充曲线”。

sentences.en: Like he just – if there's a way to be in charge, Bryce will find it in approximately 3.8 seconds and then Bryce will lord it over you.
sentences.zh: 就像他——如果有什么办法能掌权，Bryce 大约会在 3.8 秒内找到它，然后对你发号施令。

sentences.en: And so the solution to this is just be like, Bryce, shut up.
sentences.zh: 所以解决办法就是直接说：Bryce，闭嘴。

sentences.en: Like just – I knew you when you were nobody.
sentences.zh: 就像——我认识你的时候，你还什么都不是呢。

sentences.en: I'm not going to take this from you.
sentences.zh: 我可不会受你这一套。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 120, recorded on February 16th, 2023.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 120 期，录制于 2023 年 2 月 16 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host, Bryce, we continue part four of this five-part conversation with Zach Lane.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天和我的联合主持人 Bryce 一起，继续我们与 Zach Lane 五部分对话的第四部分。

sentences.en: Today we talk about safety and C++, tuples, variance, reductions, and more.
sentences.zh: 今天我们讨论安全、C++、元组、变体、归约等话题。

sentences.en: The most recent episode of Oxide and Friends, which is a podcast that I've been lamenting about her,
sentences.zh: 最近一期的《Oxide and Friends》播客，我一直在感叹的那一期，

sentences.en: it was about the – they brought on the consumer – I hope I get her name yet – right, Yale Brower.
sentences.zh: 他们请来了消费者——希望我没记错她的名字——对，Yale Brower。

sentences.en: She goes by at Yale Writes, which is Y-A-E-L on Twitter.
sentences.zh: 她在 Twitter 上的名字是 Yale Writes，拼写是 Y-A-E-L。

sentences.en: The name is Y-I-L.
sentences.zh: 名字是 Y-I-L。

sentences.en: Y-I-L.
sentences.zh: Y-I-L.

sentences.en: And so they brought her on to talk about this Rust, you know, safety, memory safety in programming languages.
sentences.zh: 他们请她来谈论 Rust，你知道的，编程语言中的安全、内存安全问题。

sentences.en: And one of the things that they actually brought up is that some analysis that – I can't remember if it was what Google did with their Android code
sentences.zh: 他们提到的其中一点是，我记不清是 Google 对他们的 Android 代码所做的分析，

sentences.en: or some other company with some – they did some analysis of, like, where the most buggy code is.
sentences.zh: 还是其他公司做的——他们分析了哪里是 Bug 最多的代码。

sentences.en: And it actually wasn't old, already existing code.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，那其实并不是陈旧的、现有的代码。

sentences.en: It was new code that was being written.
sentences.zh: 而是正在编写的新代码。

sentences.en: And so that, like, sure, there's already millions and billions of lines of C++, but, like, it actually kind of made sense when you think about it.
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然 C++ 确实已经有数以亿计的代码行了，但当你仔细想想，这其实很有道理。

sentences.en: Like, the code that's been sitting there for 20 years and kind of just working, like, maybe there's a couple bugs in it.
sentences.zh: 比如，那些已经存在了 20 年且一直运行良好的代码，可能里面确实有几个 Bug。

sentences.en: But, like, that code probably – yeah, they probably ironed out most of those bugs.
sentences.zh: 但那些代码可能——是的，它们的大部分 Bug 可能已经被修复了。

sentences.en: It's the new code that new programmers are writing.
sentences.zh: 反而是新程序员编写的新代码。

sentences.en: And, like, that's the buggiest stuff.
sentences.zh: 那才是 Bug 最多的地方。

sentences.en: So, like, if we did add that stuff, I think that, like, a majority of – like, a huge portion, at least, of bugs that are being written in C++
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们真的添加了那些东西，我认为，绝大多数——或者说很大一部分——在 C++ 中编写的 Bug

sentences.en: could be fixed by, like, new features like this kind of stuff that you're proposing, Zach.
sentences.zh: 都可以通过你提议的这类新特性来修复，Zach。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: By the way, I'm not proposing anything along those lines.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我并没有提议任何类似的东西。

sentences.en: I'm not going to get involved with the standard language changes.
sentences.zh: 我不会参与标准语言的变更。

sentences.en: That is, like, not my area.
sentences.zh: 那不是我的领域。

sentences.en: I'm not signing up.
sentences.zh: 我不会报名参加的。

sentences.en: It's like showing up on your pirate ship with a rust flag at the top of the C++ committee.
sentences.zh: 这就好比在 C++ 委员会的顶端挂上一面 Rust 的旗帜，开着海盗船闯进来。

sentences.en: But, Connor, I think that the issue is that almost every piece of new software that gets written these days uses old software and builds on top of existing things.
sentences.zh: 但是，Connor，我认为问题在于，如今编写的几乎每一款新软件都在使用旧软件，并在此基础上构建。

sentences.en: And so it may not be that there's a bug in the old code.
sentences.zh: 所以问题可能不在于旧代码中有 Bug。

sentences.en: It may be a bug in how you're using the old code.
sentences.zh: 而在于你使用旧代码的方式可能有 Bug。

sentences.en: Or it may be that you're using it in a way where, you know, there's this known sharp edge to it, but you haven't handled that in your usage of it.
sentences.zh: 或者是因为你使用它的方式存在已知的“尖锐边缘”，但你在使用时没有处理好。

sentences.en: Or you've hit a corner case that nobody else has hit before.
sentences.zh: 又或者你遇到了别人从未遇到过的边界情况。

sentences.en: Most C++ code is written with preconditions, right?
sentences.zh: 大多数 C++ 代码都是基于前提条件编写的，对吧？

sentences.en: That are sometimes stated and sometimes implicit.
sentences.zh: 有时是明确说明的，有时是隐含的。

sentences.en: And if you violate them, everything crashes, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你违反了它们，一切都会崩溃，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, womp, womp.
sentences.zh: 是的，惨了惨了。

sentences.en: What's that?
sentences.zh: 你说什么？

sentences.en: Womp, womp.
sentences.zh: 惨了惨了。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Like, you know, you're on your own, buddy.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，你自己看着办吧，伙计。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: So, you know, so you have, like, all this existing code, which might be better than new code in the sense of people who work things out.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你拥有所有这些现有的代码，从人们解决问题的角度来看，它们可能比新代码更好。

sentences.en: But it also is probably written with an eye towards performance first over safety.
sentences.zh: 但它们在编写时可能优先考虑性能而非安全性。

sentences.en: And so there's preconditions that if you don't meet, you get a crash.
sentences.zh: 所以存在一些前提条件，如果你不满足，就会导致崩溃。

sentences.en: Whereas, like, you know, the Rust model is more like, you know, there's a well-defined thing that happens and it's not a crash.
sentences.zh: 而 Rust 的模型更像是，你知道，发生的事情是有明确定义的，不会导致崩溃。

sentences.en: Even if you get, in some sense, arbitrary results, it's memory safe, right?
sentences.zh: 即使在某种意义上你得到了任意结果，它也是内存安全的，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, you know, your code is not correct because it's safe, but it's not going to, you know, bring down the airline or something.
sentences.zh: 所以，你的代码虽然不一定正确，但因为它是安全的，它不会导致航空公司系统瘫痪之类的后果。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think the problem is that there's no appetite in the C++ community for the cost that we'd have to pay for, instead of just adding library UB whenever we have, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为问题在于 C++ 社区对于我们必须付出的代价没有胃口，而不是每当我们遇到某种失败情况时，就增加库的未定义行为（UB）。

sentences.en: some failure case.
sentences.zh: 有些东西需要很快，我们不想妥善处理。

sentences.en: There's something that needs to be fast that we don't want to, you know, properly deal with.
sentences.zh: 有些东西需要很快，我们不想妥善处理。

sentences.en: The alternative would be to provide a deterministic error path.
sentences.zh: 另一种选择是提供确定性的错误路径。

sentences.en: And that oftentimes has a cost or it takes away implementation time.
sentences.zh: 但这通常是有代价的，或者会占用实现时间。

sentences.en: And we just don't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 而我们就是不想那样做。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think, I mean, I get what you're saying, but I think that there's also a lot of people that I've heard say they embrace this idea as long as it's a mode, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我明白你的意思，但我认为我也听过很多人说，只要它是一种模式，他们就接受这个想法，对吧？

sentences.en: So in other words,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，

sentences.en: just like Rust has this get out of jail free card where you could just say unsafe and then you can go down to the bit twiddling that you need to do in some cases.
sentences.zh: 就像 Rust 有这种“免死金牌”，你可以直接说 unsafe，然后在某些情况下进行必要的位操作。

sentences.en: And then everything's built on top of, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后一切都建立在那个基础上，你知道，

sentences.en: that becomes the old legacy code that's been hardened because everyone's been depending on it using it so hard for such a long time.
sentences.zh: 那变成了经过强化的旧遗留代码，因为每个人都已经依赖它并长时间高强度地使用它了。

sentences.en: You figure to have all those errors that might be in there.
sentences.zh: 你认为里面可能存在的错误都已经被找出来了。

sentences.en: And then the new stuff that you write on top is like very, very carefully vetted by the borrow checking kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后你在上面编写的新东西，会受到借用检查机制非常非常仔细的审查。

sentences.en: It does make me think if we wanted to introduce a mode, a deterministic error mode for the standard library where all the error cases would give you some, you know,
sentences.zh: 这确实让我想到，如果我们想引入一种模式，一种针对标准库的确定性错误模式，如果违反了前提条件，所有的错误情况都会给你某种异常或全局中止之类的反馈，

sentences.en: exception or global board or something if a precondition is violated.
sentences.zh: 那我们能消除多少库的未定义行为呢？

sentences.en: How much library UB would we be able to get rid of?
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能认为我们可以消除所有这些行为，但肯定有些情况下，前提条件非常难以检查，甚至是不可能检查的。

sentences.en: Now, you might think we'd get rid of all of it, but there are certainly some cases where there's a precondition that's very difficult to check or impossible to check.
sentences.zh: 或者有时是不可能的，是的。

sentences.en: Or sometimes impossible, yeah.
sentences.zh: 有些检查在字面上是不可判定的。

sentences.en: Some of those checks are literally undecidable.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，如果我们有一种模式来检查我们能检查的东西，我们会获得多少实用价值。

sentences.en: But I wonder how much utility we would have from checking the things that we, from having a mode that checks the things that we can.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，如果我们有一种模式来检查我们能检查的东西，我们会获得多少实用价值。

sentences.en: I think a lot.
sentences.zh: 我认为会很多。

sentences.en: So I think the way that you get value here is you'd have to have a safe mode and then you'd have to have some minimal subset of C++ libraries,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为获得价值的方法是，你必须有一个安全模式，然后你必须有一个 C++ 库的最小子集，

sentences.en: of the C++ library that is safe mode friendly, right?
sentences.zh: 即对安全模式友好的 C++ 库，对吧？

sentences.en: So I think, you know, I've been telling anyone who will listen, I think really should have about four containers and everything else should be an adapter.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，我一直在告诉任何愿意听的人，我认为我们真的应该只有大约四个容器，其他一切都应该是适配器。

sentences.en: So we should have like a map kind of thing, actually, but the map should be like a hash map, like a high quality open addressing hash map.
sentences.zh: 所以我们应该有一种类似 map 的东西，实际上，map 应该像哈希表，比如高质量的开放寻址哈希表。

sentences.en: And then we should have like a vector and then, you know, a couple other things, right?
sentences.zh: 然后我们应该有 vector，还有其他一些东西，对吧？

sentences.en: Because I don't think people really care about linked lists and node-based containers very much these days.
sentences.zh: 因为我不认为现在人们真的关心链表和基于节点的容器。

sentences.en: And so you need like this foundation of really efficient by construction things that are like very contiguous and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要这种由高效构造组成的基石，它们非常连续等等。

sentences.en: So if we added like a couple of those basic building blocks and then had, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们添加了几个这样的基本构建块，然后你就可以使用像算法这样的东西，因为大概内存安全的东西能够检查，在你的特定算法实例化中，

sentences.en: you could use things like the algorithms because like presumably the memory safe thing would be able to check like in your particular instantiation of this algorithm,
sentences.zh: 当它运行时，是否有内存安全问题，然后你就可以使用这些东西，见招拆招，

sentences.en: when it runs, does it have memory safety problems or not, then you'd be able to use stuff, catch as catch can,
sentences.zh: 你可能会随着时间的推移引入新的算法，它们有略微不同的要求和略微不同的保证。

sentences.en: and you'd maybe introduce new algorithms over time that have slightly different requirements and slightly different guarantees.
sentences.zh: 但确实，我认为必须有库的支持，绝对必须，事情才能奏效。

sentences.en: But yeah, there has to be library support for it, I think, absolutely, for things to work.
sentences.zh: 但我想我们能做到。

sentences.en: But I think we can get there.
sentences.zh: 困难的部分在于让演进团队，也就是语言侧的人，去接受一个非常非常大的语言特性。

sentences.en: The difficult part becomes getting the evolution folks, the language side folks to bite off a very, very large language feature.
sentences.zh: 那总是一场艰苦的战斗，不是因为他们脾气暴躁，不想这样做，对吧？

sentences.en: And that's always an uphill battle, not because they're, you know, grumpy and don't want it, right?
sentences.zh: 总是因为他们必须通盘考虑，因为一旦你把它放入标准，就很难再改变任何东西了。

sentences.en: It's always because they have to think through everything because once you put it into the standard, it's very hard to change anything.
sentences.zh: 我们通常会被我们标准化的语义所束缚。

sentences.en: And we're usually stuck with the semantics that we standardize.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想确保做得正确，这是可以理解的。

sentences.en: So they want to make sure they get it right and that's understandable.
sentences.zh: 所以你有类似的东西，比如我们得到的概念（Concepts）版本，我认为花了大约两个半发布周期，也就是三年。

sentences.en: So you have things like, you know, like the version of concepts we got was, I think, about two and a half cycles in the making of release cycles, you know, three years.
sentences.zh: 然后，协程（Coroutines）也差不多，两到三个周期，模块（Modules）花了超过三个周期。

sentences.en: And then, you know, co-routines was about the same, two or three modules was more than three.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些具有巨大影响的大型语言特性，基本上所有这些在 C++20 中落地的东西，因为它们在路线图上已经很久了，

sentences.en: So, you know, these big language features that have like a large impact, basically all these things that landed in 20 because they were on the roadmap for a long time,
sentences.zh: 这也会是其中之一。

sentences.en: this would be another one of those.
sentences.zh: 所以你在谈论的是，如果有人现在正在研究它，并且他们正在做一个在 Clang 或 GCC 等编译器中工作的实现，

sentences.en: And so you're talking about like, you know, if someone was working on that right now and they're making an implementation that worked in Clang or GCC or something,
sentences.zh: 标准化它需要多长时间？

sentences.en: how long would it take to standardize that?
sentences.zh: 我们在谈论的是，那是一个 32 或 35 标准。

sentences.en: We're talking about like, you know, that's a, that's a, that's a 20, I mean, that's a 32 or 35.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为我们在委员会经常开玩笑说，库小组移动得更快，能完成很多事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, we, I think we, we joke often on the committee that, you know, the library group, you know, moves faster, gets, gets a lot of things done.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，我认为我们经常，库流水线通常对等待未来语言特性的承诺不感兴趣，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: And more importantly, I think we often, the library pipeline is often uninterested in, in waiting for the promise of a future language feature because, you know,
sentences.zh: 它们往往无法实现，或者需要很长时间才能实现。

sentences.en: oftentimes they don't materialize or they take a long time to materialize.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是因为语言演进小组没有做同样多的工作。

sentences.en: And in no way is this because the language evolution group isn't doing as much work.
sentences.zh: 只是因为你必须做更多的工作才能把它放入语言中。

sentences.en: It's just because you have to do a lot more work to put it into the language.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是我们在库中做很多事情的原因之一，而这些事情在语言中做可能会更好。

sentences.en: And that's actually, you know, that's, that's one of the reasons why we do a lot of things in the library that other link that, that maybe would be better done in the language.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们在库中可以移动得更快。

sentences.en: And it's because we can move, move faster in the library.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: Um, yeah.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果库里有什么你不喜欢的，就别用它。

sentences.en: And, and if there's something that you don't like in the library, just don't use it.
sentences.zh: 而语言语义一旦确定，你就被困住了。

sentences.en: Whereas a language semantic, you're stuck with it.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 语言级元组。

sentences.en: Language tuples.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们应该这样做。

sentences.en: Yeah, we should.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 那个，那个，我们本应该做语言级元组的。

sentences.en: That one, that one, we should have done language tuple.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对应该做语言级元组。

sentences.en: We definitely should have done language tuple.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们有语言级变体和语言级元组。

sentences.en: I wish we had language variant language tuple.
sentences.zh: 我只是，特别是在你谈论 Haskell 之后，我就觉得，这是我从不谈论的另一件事，就是，

sentences.en: I just, I was like, especially after you were talking about Haskell and like, I was like, that's the, another thing I never talk about is like,
sentences.zh: 没有代数数据类型，我很难在一种语言中工作。

sentences.en: it's so hard for me to work in a language without algebraic data types.
sentences.zh: 就像，我们有乘积类型，但有一半的语言到此为止了。

sentences.en: And like, it's like, we have product types, but then like half the languages stop there.
sentences.zh: 还有一些和类型，呃，我们会给你一些类似联合体的东西。

sentences.en: And there are like some types, eh, we'll give you some like unions or something like that.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你使用它们，特别是当它设计了非常好的模式匹配时，它就是那种东西。

sentences.en: But it's like, once you use them, especially when it's designed with really nice pattern matching, it's just, it's, it's very, it's one of those things.
sentences.zh: 在你的语言中没有那个真的很难受。

sentences.en: It's very hard to, to not have that in your language.
sentences.zh: 这，嗯，现在我们要有 std::variant 了，然后我们可能还会有 L-variant，呃，这将是语言级的。

sentences.en: Which, um, which is now we're going to have stood variant and then we might have L variant and, uh, which is going to be the language.
sentences.zh: 因为我不知道。

sentences.en: Cause I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我看到在某个时候有人提议，我，我，是的，确实有提议，但目前没有任何正在进行中的方案。

sentences.en: I saw at some point someone was proposing a, I'm, I'm, I, yeah, there, there have been proposals, but there's no, there are, there are none that are in flight right now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，语言级变体很好。

sentences.en: You know, a language variant is nice.
sentences.zh: 我更关心拥有语言级元组。

sentences.en: I care far more about having a language tuple.
